questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Calder Pet Products, a privately held firm decides to ignore differences among buyers in Hillcrest and offer one product with one marketing mix aimed at the whole market. Which targeting strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Undifferentiated, or mass, marketing treats the whole market as one group and uses a single offer and message. It assumes buyers share enough needs that one approach works. Differentiated marketing would design separate offers for several segments, concentrated marketing would target one segment, and micromarketing would tailor to individuals or very local groups.
questions.hint: Ask whether the firm treats everyone the same or tailors the offer.

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: For Glenmark Pharmaceuticals, a startup firm, a perceptual map of the Westmoor market plots brands on price (budget to premium) and service level (low to high). Most competitors cluster in the budget, low service corner, leaving the opposite corner empty. What does the empty corner suggest for the firm?
questions.explanation: A perceptual map shows how brands are positioned in customers' minds on key dimensions. A cluster of competitors in one corner with an empty opposite corner suggests a possible gap, a position few brands occupy, which could be an opportunity if enough buyers want it. An empty spot does not prove there is no demand; it may mean the combination has simply not been offered. The map is a tool for spotting exactly this kind of opening.
questions.hint: Read the empty space as a possible gap, not as proof of no demand.
questions.learningObjective: read a perceptual map for positioning gaps
